transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14 10:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (CEO), Ethan (CTO), Lina (VP Product), Marcus (Head of Infra), Sophie (Head of People), Jon (Head of Sales), plus all-hands on stream

Summary notes and auto sections may be imperfect.

[00:00:00] Maya: All right good morning team, thanks for joining. I know folks are dialing in from EMEA later so we'll keep to ninety minutes no, sorry, 60. Um quick agenda, incident recap, Q1 priorities, hiring notes, open floor.

[00:00:18] Ethan: Quick note, we'll start with the incident, Marcus will run through timeline then open to questions.

[00:00:25] Marcus: Cool. So on Feb 7th we saw a latency spike across a subset of hosted clusters — primarily in us-west-2. It started around 02:10 UTC and lasted about 37 minutes, we had automatic fallback to lower-tier model variants which mitigated errors but some tail latency remained. Root cause: a combination of a kernel-level change pushed with a perf regression and an unanticipated sequence-length distribution for a major customer workload.

[00:01:05] Lina: Just to clarify, was the regression triggered by the compilation/kernel selector path or by the runtime batching heuristics?

[00:01:12] Marcus: It appears to be the kernel selection, specifically on our newer integer-quantized path — something about register allocation changed performance on long-context sequences. The batching heuristics exacerbated it because they fed longer sequences into that codepath more often.

[00:01:33] Ethan: Right, and we rolled back the kernel optimization within 18 minutes once we saw the signal. The compensating fallback routing helped, but not everything switched immediately. We need faster automatic routing to live-compatible variants.

[00:01:49] Maya: Big takeaway — we need clearer guardrails for any optimization that touches kernel selection. The product velocity playbook can't outpace our safety checks.

[00:02:01] Sophie: There's also a people side here — on-call load was high, and several ICs were pinged off-hours. We need a cadence for incident rotation so we avoid burnout.

[00:02:12] Jon: Customers were impacted, a few enterprise customers flagged higher latencies; CS handled triage and sent notes, but we should standardize the external comms.

[00:02:25] [00:02:30] Speaker 1 (transcription glitch): um hh we uh sort of patch — the the fallback wasn't uniform and, yeah, some calls timed out —

[00:02:38] Lina: Okay, proposed actions — suspend any remaining kernels-in-flight until we have canary thresholds and perf signatures; expand test coverage for long-context sequences in our CI, and add explicit gating for quantized kernel paths.

[00:02:56] Marcus: Agree. I'll own the RCA doc and will list follow-ups. Also recommend a very small canary window (5-10% traffic) and an automatic rollback triggered by p50/p95 deviations beyond a threshold.

[00:03:12] Ethan: We should also add synthetic workload tests that mirror big customers' sequence distributions. Right now our synthetic tests skew shorter. That's a test coverage gap.

[00:03:23] Maya: Good. On the product side, Lina — how does this affect the Q1 roadmap?

[00:03:29] Lina: We have two major milestones: a cache-enhanced batching feature and the new routing policy for dedicated customers. Given the incident, I propose we delay the cache-enhanced release by two sprints to harden quantized path testing. We keep the routing policy but make it opt-in for early customers.

[00:03:46] Jon: From sales — customers want predictable latency and explicit SLOs; some were asking for dedicated pools or VPC/private options to isolate workload variance. We should be careful with messaging — don't oversell zero-risk.

[00:04:02] Maya: Messaging note captured. Also we need to be explicit about what our SLA covers and what the prescriptive mitigations are.

[00:04:10] [00:04:12] Speaker 2 (crowd noise): so um, can we get a cheat sheet for CS yes or no on feature rollouts?

[00:04:18] Sophie: I'll produce interim guidance for customer-facing teams — what to say in the first 24 hours and what the follow-up cadence is.

[00:04:26] Marcus: Quick technical ask — our KV cache eviction heuristics need reviewing. We saw cache thrash when we switched back and that amplified tail latency.

[00:04:36] Ethan: Agreed. We'll instrument more metrics around cache miss patterns and add a throttle to eviction.

[00:04:44] Lina: On velocity vs guardrails — I want to propose three concrete rules: 1) any kernel-level change must pass long-context perf signatures, 2) canary windows must be at least 5% for 30 minutes plus automatic rollback criteria, 3) preflight tests must include synthetic traffic that mirrors top-3 customer patterns.

[00:05:06] Maya: Those are good. Any objections?

[00:05:09] [00:05:11] Ethan: No objections; implementation details belong to infra and product engineering.

[00:05:15] Jon: Quick question re: Dedicated customers — do we need to change pricing or offer an SLA uplift option? Some customers signalled willingness to pay for reserved pools with tighter SLOs.

[00:05:26] Maya: Let's capture that in pricing follow-up. Jon, can you pull the top five asks and price sensitivity?

[00:05:33] Jon: Yep will do.

[00:05:36] Sophie: Hiring — heads up, we're not freezing roles but we'll triage open reqs and pause non-critical roles for 30 days while we evaluate runway and priorities. I'll publish the list and temporary hiring rubric tomorrow.

[00:05:48] Maya: Keep us posted. I want to be transparent with the company about runway decisions but also not cause panic.

[00:05:57] [00:06:00] Crowd: a few murmurs, uh okay, thanks Maya

[00:06:05] Lina: Back to product — we also need better telemetry for rollouts: a single dashboard that shows p50/p95/p99 per-model, per-region, and rollout cohort. The console should surface automatic rollback suggestions.

[00:06:18] Marcus: We have partial data in tracing but it's fragmented. We'll put a small cross-team task force together to build that dashboard.

[00:06:27] Ethan: On the technical debt side — there are three infra items that are high priority: kernel selector refactor, KV cache tuning, and canary automation. We should reallocate a sprint worth of cycles.

[00:06:39] Maya: Ok reallocation noted. This is the tension — we want speed but not at the expense of calling the team at 2am.

[00:06:47] [00:07:00] Speaker 3 (slightly garbled): um earlier you mentioned audit logs, is that part of this?

[00:07:03] Lina: Not directly, but auditability matters for enterprise customers. We should ensure our rollback and routing decisions are recorded in audit logs for compliance.

[00:07:12] Sophie: Also tie this into SSO & RBAC changes; when we add canary control panels, we need role gating so only specific folks can flip a flag.

[00:07:20] Maya: Good point.

[00:07:24] Jon: Competitor note — MegaCloud AI recently announced extended SLAs and some new routing features. We shouldn't chase every feature, but we need to be explicit where Redwood differentiates: observability, cost controls, and unified deployment modes.

[00:07:39] Ethan: We'll draft a positioning paragraph for marketing: what we commit to in an SLA and how we manage rollouts.

[00:07:46] [00:08:00] Crowd reaction, typing

[00:08:05] Maya: All right, open floor quick Q&A — please keep questions short.

[00:08:12] Speaker 4 (Engineer): For the canary thresholds, are we thinking absolute latency numbers or delta from baseline?

[00:08:18] Marcus: Delta from baseline with absolute upper bounds. So if p95 increases > 25% OR absolute p95 > 500ms we rollback. We can refine after first runs.

[00:08:31] Speaker 5 (PM): Are we changing how we do feature flags vs model rollouts?

[00:08:36] Lina: We'll unify the control plane so model rollouts and feature flags share canary infrastructure and visibility.

[00:08:42] Speaker 6 (Support): For customer comms, what's the defined timeline to notify?

[00:08:47] Sophie: Initial notification within 60 minutes for incidents affecting SLAs, and a follow-up within 24 hours. I'll standardize language.

[00:08:55] [00:09:10] Speaker 7 (joke): Are we doing chocolates at after-hours on-call?

[00:09:12] Sophie: We'll do better than chocolates — proper rotation and time-off compensation.

[00:09:20] Maya: Okay final items: we want measurable guardrails and a clear story to customers. I'll ask Lina and Marcus to produce a short doc that we can share with customers explaining our rollback and canary philosophy.

[00:09:34] Lina: We'll draft and ship by end of week.

[00:09:38] Marcus: RCA doc also by EOD Friday.

[00:09:42] Jon: Sales to get the messaging and top asks list by Thursday.

[00:09:47] Sophie: Hiring guidance and interim comms tomorrow.

[00:09:50] Maya: Great. Quick pulse — how confident are we about shipping the refined rollout system by end of Q1? Quick raise hands.

[00:09:58] [00:10:10] (several hands in the video grid, murmurs)

[00:10:15] Ethan: We'll probably get a v1 by end of Q1 if we prioritize it — v1 meaning basic canary automation and dashboard.

[00:10:23] Maya: ok that's the plan. Any final questions?

[00:10:30] Speaker 8 (Finance): Does this materially change expected spend on infra?

[00:10:35] Marcus: Short term maybe a bump for more synthetic testing and dedicated canary capacity, but we expect overall savings from fewer incidents and smarter routing within a quarter.

[00:10:46] Maya: All right thanks everyone. We'll share notes, the RCA, the Q1 priorities doc, and the hiring guidance in the company channel. Please check the action items. Meeting adjourned.

[00:10:58] (informal wrap-up and small-group follow-ups continue off-record)

End of transcript. Some speaker labels and timings may be approximate due to transcription artifacts.
